rule.description: Every function that directly mutates a field of the per-activity activity audit record (the audit* fields of struct android_app: auditLastStage, auditTransitions, auditStampMs, auditSuppressed) in its own body is one owner of the record's entry protocol. Two or more distinct owner functions across the analyzed translation units mean the record is owned by no single place: any change to the entry protocol must be repeated once per owning function.

checks.description: A function directly mutates a field of the activity audit record (auditLastStage, auditTransitions, auditStampMs, auditSuppressed) in its own body instead of delegating to one shared recording path. clang-tidy check smellbench-audit-ownership reports each such function once per translation unit, together with the mutated fields, the number of direct writes and the location of the first one; smell_check.sh compiles the three relevant translation units (activity glue, USB permission helper, WebView implementation block) and takes the union of distinct writer function names.
checks.detected_relation: function body -> inlined mutation of an audit* record field
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The record implements one conceptual entry protocol - classify the step, count it or fold it, stamp it - but that protocol is restated in-line in every function that files an entry, so any protocol change is a cross-file edit repeated once per writing function. The canonical repair funnels every mutation through one writer function, whatever it is called and wherever it lives, and the relation then matches exactly once instead of 38 times.

matches.evidence: Filing the SAVE_STATE handover directly: `auditLastStage = APP_CMD_SAVE_STATE;` followed by `auditTransitions += 1;` inside the saved-state release path.

Both polled-command sides update the record inline: the success path folds repeats with `auditSuppressed += ( auditLastStage == cmd );` before tagging `auditLastStage = cmd;`, and the empty-pipe path sets `auditLastStage = AUDIT_STAGE_ANOMALOUS; auditSuppressed++;`.

The largest restatement of the entry protocol spread over six switch cases: tag + increment on four commands, a private CLOCK_MONOTONIC milliseconds block for APP_CMD_INIT_WINDOW, and a read-gated choice between `auditTransitions++` and `auditSuppressed++` for the lifecycle states.

Three more inline restatements: TERM_WINDOW is tagged and then folded via `auditSuppressed++;`, SAVE_STATE counts with `auditTransitions = auditTransitions + 1;` (a third counting spelling), and RESUME resets `auditSuppressed = 0;` after tagging.

Teardown restates its own timestamp block (`clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, ...)` to milliseconds into `auditStampMs`) before tagging `auditLastStage = AUDIT_STAGE_TEARDOWN;` and incrementing the transition counter.
The UI-thread consumer tags the cross-thread handoff inline through the global path: `gapp->auditLastStage = AUDIT_STAGE_UI_DISPATCH; gapp->auditTransitions++;`.
The app-thread dispatcher opens every command dispatch with its own timestamp block plus `auditLastStage = cmd;` and `auditTransitions += 1;`, taken from the polled command value.

Frame zero of the record is built inline here: `auditLastStage = AUDIT_STAGE_LAUNCH;` along with explicit re-zeroing of `auditTransitions` and `auditSuppressed` and a full CLOCK_MONOTONIC block into `auditStampMs`.
Cold-start versus restore is decided with an if/else that tags `AUDIT_STAGE_RESTORED` or `AUDIT_STAGE_LAUNCH` directly and then increments the transition counter.
The main-thread request side files its own entry with `auditLastStage = cmd; auditTransitions++;` before the pipe write.
After the acknowledgement wait loop, tags `auditLastStage = APP_CMD_INPUT_CHANGED;` and increments the counter inline.
Tags the direction the window moved with a conditional expression (`( window != NULL ) ? APP_CMD_INIT_WINDOW : APP_CMD_TERM_WINDOW;`) instead of a plain value, then increments the counter.
After the state-acknowledgement wait loop, files the confirmed state inline via `auditLastStage = cmd; auditTransitions++;`.
The final entry is filed inline right before the object becomes unusable: `auditLastStage = AUDIT_STAGE_TEARDOWN; auditTransitions++;`.
The main-thread destroy callback now extracts `activity->instance` into a local purely to tag `AUDIT_STAGE_TEARDOWN` and increment the counter before the shared teardown path runs.
Start callback tags `APP_CMD_START` through a newly introduced local `android_app` and increments the counter inline.
Resume callback mutates the record without any local at all: two `((struct android_app*)activity->instance)->audit...` statements before delegating to the shared state-setter.

Save-state callback duplicates the fold-or-count decision inline: if the current record stage is not SAVE_STATE it increments `auditTransitions`, otherwise it increments `auditSuppressed`, then retags.
Pause callback tags `APP_CMD_PAUSE` through the cast-expression path and increments the counter inline.
Stop callback tags `APP_CMD_STOP` through a newly introduced local `android_app` and increments the counter inline.
Tag-only entry: the callback sets `auditLastStage = APP_CMD_CONFIG_CHANGED;` inline and increments nothing, relying on the app thread to count.
Second tag-only entry, same shape as configuration changes: `auditLastStage = APP_CMD_LOW_MEMORY;` inline.

Focus callback tags through a conditional expression on `focused` and then counts with a third spelling: `auditTransitions += auditStampMs ? 1 : 0;`, i.e. the fold decision is keyed off the timestamp field being set.

Window creation carries its own inline timestamp block (the same CLOCK_MONOTONIC-to-milliseconds computation written out a third time, here through a local `android_app`) before tagging `APP_CMD_INIT_WINDOW` and counting.
Window teardown tags `APP_CMD_TERM_WINDOW` through a local `android_app` and increments the counter inline, a fourth distinct combination of stage value and access path.
Tags the raw `APP_CMD_INPUT_CHANGED` inline and counts the transition through a newly introduced local `android_app`.

Records the opposite direction (queue destroyed) with the exact same inline statements as E26 - same tag `APP_CMD_INPUT_CHANGED`, same counter increment - so the two directions are indistinguishable in the record.
Fold-only entry through the raw cast-expression path: `((struct android_app*)activity->instance)->auditSuppressed++;` - redraw storms are folded rather than counted, with no stage tag at all.

The producer side of the UI-thread handoff duplicates the consumer's entry one-to-one (`gapp->auditLastStage = AUDIT_STAGE_UI_DISPATCH; gapp->auditTransitions++;`), with a tab-indented inline comment on the increment.
The USB disconnect helper files an entry directly into the glue's record through the global path: `gapp->auditLastStage = AUDIT_STAGE_USB_EVENT; gapp->auditTransitions++;`.

The permission round is audited inline at two internal points of one long JNI flow: tag + count before opening the device, and a separate `gapp->auditSuppressed++;` in the `!deviceConnection` refusal branch.

Files its entry as late as possible after the shared JNI attach preamble: `gapp->auditLastStage = AUDIT_STAGE_WEBVIEW_EVENT; gapp->auditTransitions++;` - the first of seven per-function copies inside the WebView implementation block.
Progress polling writes a fold-only entry on the hot path - `gapp->auditSuppressed++;` with no stage tag - attempting to keep the churn visible without counting each poll.

Message posts branch the fold decision on the function argument: `if( initial ) gapp->auditTransitions++; else gapp->auditSuppressed++;` after tagging - a per-call classification the other sites do not use.
Canvas draws tag and count inline before the JNI call, with a comment noting canvas draws are exactly what page-change reports need.
Pixel reads tag and count inline even though pixel reads are not lifecycle steps; the comment records that they used to be folded before field support asked for them counted.
Tags and counts each JavaScript hop inline right after the attach preamble, the same two statements as E32/E35/E36.

The title fetch holds a tag-only entry (`gapp->auditLastStage = AUDIT_STAGE_WEBVIEW_EVENT;`), yet records the same stage as each create, draw, pixel read and script hop, so the entries cannot be told apart.

excluded.reason: The input-event dispatcher was deliberately left record-free: per-event audit would flood an in-place record without serving the feature, so it is a naturally adjacent non-matching neighbor, not a credited site.
Its body is a commented-out debug block with no live statements; no record code could be placed there.

excluded.symbol: stateSaved / destroyRequested / destroyed / redrawNeeded / activityState / running
excluded.reason: These are pre-existing functional control-flow fields of the glue, not part of the audit record. The rule matches only mutations of audit* fields; mutations of these fields elsewhere in the same functions are not part of the relation.

excluded.symbol: struct android_app (audit* field declarations); enum AUDIT_STAGE_*
excluded.reason: Declarations only. The rule reports functions whose bodies mutate the record; type definitions and the stage vocabulary have no function context and cannot be writers.
Mutations of these module globals in DisconnectUSB and RequestPermissionOrGetConnectionFD steer real behavior (reconnect backoff and connection state) and are not audit* record fields.
Mutations of the WebView bookkeeping struct are not mutations of the activity audit record carried on struct android_app.
Surveys the registration point but files no entry itself; entry filing for creation is covered by android_app_create and the app-thread entry frame. Unchanged, so it is neither an entry nor a match.
